facts.fact: maCERT, the DGSSI's cyber watch and response centre, issued a security warning bulletin (ref. 65471806/26) on the FortiBleed leak affecting Fortinet firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, saying several Moroccan institutions were affected and urging MFA and password changes.
maCERT is described as the DGSSI's centre for vigilance, monitoring and response to cyber attacks, operating under the National Defence Administration.
The strategy states Morocco adopted its first national cybersecurity strategy in 2012.

The DGSSI publishes the Stratégie Nationale de Cybersécurité 2030 as the successor to the 2012 strategy, with 4 pillars, 11 objectives, 26 initiatives and 60 actions; the document is undated and its date here is the 2024 published proxy.
The strategy's legal timeline states Décret n° 2-11-509 created the DGSSI in 2011.
The DGSSI is stated to have updated the national information security directive (DNSSI v2.0, Circulaire 2/2023) drawing on its own control, audit and incident-handling actions across organisations.

note: Directive scope covers vital-importance infrastructures but states no designation or incident reporting duty to the body.

facts.fact: The op-ed says Morocco has a national cybersecurity strategy to 2030, alongside Law 05.20 and national information-systems security directives.
The op-ed names the DGSSI as the national body for framing, security watch, auditing and incident response, operating the maCERT.

The op-ed cites data given to Parliament in November 2025 that the DGSSI detected 879 cyber incidents, 109 of which required its direct intervention, and says it confirmed the 2025 Tawtik.ma data leak.

The DGSSI count of 879 incidents detected, with no period given, and audits finding critical flaws in 20 of 76 applications in the first nine months of 2025, were presented to Parliament in November 2025.

facts.fact: Minister Delegate Abdeltif Loudiyi told the House of Representatives committee that the DGSSI carries out its annual monitoring and audit programme under Law 05.20 on cybersecurity, and that it is implementing the national cybersecurity strategy to 2030.
Loudiyi said the DGSSI's watch and response centre received 419 reports of possible incidents from January to September 2026, 123 needing direct intervention, 47 with digital forensic analysis.

Loudiyi said the DGSSI produced in 2026 the results of its study of critical infrastructures' compliance with cybersecurity legal requirements and began helping them identify, classify and declare their sensitive systems.

Loudiyi said the centre proactively notified the bodies concerned of 2,154 security threats and issued 968 bulletins in 2026, 373 of them critical, and the 123 interventions in the January to September 2026 period.
